facts.text: New Oxford was originally platted in 1792 for Henry Kuhn and named “Oxford town” because a nearby ford and a local tavern called Dutch Frederick’s stand featured an ox’s head.
The New Oxford Area Historical Society preserves and celebrates the borough’s heritage, welcoming visitors into a charming historic building filled with stories and artifacts.
Sandridge Crafted Foods, Yazoo Mills, Pilgrim’s Pride, and Aero Energy are among the large manufacturing plants that give New Oxford a diverse industrial base.
Every year the New Oxford Chamber of Commerce hosts an antiques and crafts show on the third Saturday in June, drawing collectors from the region.
The Historical Society’s programs combine meticulous research, engaging events, and educational outreach to connect the past with the present for visitors of all ages.
New Oxford’s location at 39°51′48″N 77°3′23″W places it in the rolling hills of Adams County, Pennsylvania.
